Compares the last 7 days with the longer run of weeks before them. 0.80 - 1.30 is the usual range. This is load guidance, not a prediction of injury.
Calculated by Apex from your daily heart-rate load.
Not enough days of heart-rate data yet to show training load.

Strain measures the cardiovascular load of your day on a 0 to 21 scale, from the time you spend at higher heart rates. The scale is not linear: each point is harder to earn than the last. It is Apex\'s own derived number.
Each minute of heart rate above 30 percent of your reserve adds load, and harder minutes add disproportionately more. The day\'s load is the sum of those minutes.
Zones are set at 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90 percent of your maximum heart rate.
Your Strain Target is a range of one point either side of a centre set from today\'s Recovery. A Recovery of 0 percent points to 6, 50 percent to 12 and 100 percent to 18.
Training load uses a 7-day and a 28-day average of daily load. Monotony is the 7-day mean divided by its spread; a high value means very similar days.
Today\'s strain is provisional until the day ends.
